title: Review of c33's phoretic swim-then-divide (SIMD): replicated on seeds 5 and 6; 2 of 46 and 1 of 43 dividing parents travel >= 3 diameters merger-free before splitting, both daughters capped
summary: World copied unchanged. labkit seed 5 (t=400): composites from the uniform particle mix, 12 persistent splits, generation 3 (merge/split 1.48). The claim's screen.py + lineage.py on new seeds 5 and 6 to t=800: 46 and 43 persistent splits, generation 7 on both; 41/46 and 40/43 with both daughters carrying B. Merger-free travel of the parent between its own birth (or last merge) and its split: >= 3 cluster diameters in 2 of 46 on seed 5 (track 317: 5.3 diameters, 47 -> 27 + 19, B share 0.26/0.21, swimdivide_s5_track317.png; track 34: 4.9 diameters) and 1 of 43 on seed 6 (track 211: 4.0 diameters, 95 -> 64 + 31). Rare, as the claim says (2, 0, 1 per seed there).

observations.S: scr_s5.png first panel and rerun/seed5/particles.png t=0: uniform random particle mix
observations.I: scr_s5.png, scr_s6.png: discrete Janus composites (A body, B cap) in a food gas
observations.M: swimdivide_s5_track317.png: track 317 travels 5.3 own cluster diameters merger-free (t~556-670) with its B cap held; lin_s5.txt also track 34 (4.9); lin_s6.txt track 211 (4.0). Counts of all dividing tracks: 2/46 (seed 5) and 1/43 (seed 6) pass in cluster diameters (1.8 sqrt(n/pi), the round-body unit); labkit's sqrt(area) screen was not used for this count
observations.D: lin_s5.txt / lin_s6.txt: 46 and 43 persistent splits, generation 7 on both seeds, 41/46 and 40/43 with B in both daughters; track 317 splits 47 -> 27 + 19

verdicts.limitation: Swim-then-divide is rare (1-2 of 43-46 divisions per seed); most divisions come from composites that grew by merging. Merges outnumber splits (genealogy reticulate). Diameters are particle-cluster diameters, not labkit body lengths (labkit's tracker on the rendered field gives only generation 3 with merge/split 1.48 at t=400). I did not run the reciprocal twin.
